title: Throughput Contract Orchestrator for regional shard balancing, commitment-based autoscaling, and residency-safe failback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a Throughput Contract Orchestrator that guarantees committed throughput per customer across regional and multi-zone dedicated fleets, enforces data residency constraints during placement, and provides predictable, safe failback when capacity or region preferences are violated.

Background: Customers on Redwood Dedicated purchase or reserve committed throughput for business-critical LLM workloads. Current autoscaling is reactive and region-unaware: under regional outages or imbalanced demand, we either overprovision or silently redirect traffic, risking SLA violations or data-sovereignty breaches. We need a scheduler that translates throughput commitments into shard-level allocations, pre-warms capacity, and orchestrates graceful failback with residency-safe routing annotations.

Scope:
- Contract model: commitments expressed as throughput units (tokens/sec) per region (or regional pair) with optional zone preferences.
- Allocator: convert commitments into shard weights and pin shards to multi-zone placements with residency labels.
- Prefetch/Prewarm: create short-lived prewarm leases to avoid cold start spikes when commitments are first used or scaled.
- Autoscale contracts: a hybrid policy combining reserved throughput (hard guarantee) with elastic headroom (soft buffer) and cool-down windows.
- Failback & failover: safe fallback path that preserves residency constraints; when capacity unavailable in region, orchestrator executes staged spillback to approved fallback regions with timeouts and customer notifications.
- Admission controls: placement checks that enforce KMS/HSM residency flags and audit logging for any cross-residency routing.

Non-goals: full UI console surfaces (we'll expose initial controls via API and CLI), rewriting runtime kernel selection, or changing billing models in this iteration.
acceptance_criteria: Commitment API: create/update/delete of regional throughput contracts via API with validation and residency flags.
Allocator: scheduler maps contracts to shard allocations such that 95% of committed throughput is available with headroom within 90s of load ramp for staged workloads.
Prefetch: first-request latency improvement on cold scale-up events of >= 30% vs baseline for committed capacity paths.
Residency enforcement: no committed-shard accepts requests that violate customer residency flags; cross-region routing must produce an auditable exception and explicit customer opt-in.
Failback playbook: automated staged failback executed in simulated regional outage test with developer-observed graceful degradation (no >5% request loss, and error budget alerts fire correctly).
Telemetry: per-contract metrics available in Console (committed_throughput, allocated_shards, prewarm_leases, residency_violations, failback_events).
Security: design passes security review and audit-log schema approved by Security team.
implementation_plan: Design contract schema and API -> Confluence design doc linked in attachments.
Proto scheduler service: implement mapping of throughput -> shard_weights + placement constraints.
Integrate prewarm lease controller into cluster autoscaler to create short-lived reserved pods for committed shards.
Admission controller: enforce residency flags and surface humane errors to upstream routing layer.
Failback orchestrator: implement staged spillover with cooldowns, notification hooks, and circuit-breakers.
Metrics + tracing: instrument key decision points and add dashboards/alerts.
E2E tests: chaos + regional simulation, load ramp tests, and regression tests for residency enforcement.
Gradual rollout: start with internal customers -> limited beta -> general availability.
Docs + SDK: API docs, example terraform/CLI snippets, and runbook for SRE/CS teams.
Post-launch: iterate on headroom tuning and cost accounting for prewarm leases.
work_items: Prewarm controller: lease lifecycle manager - ENG-811217-03
Failback: staged spillover state machine - ENG-811217-05
monitoring_and_slo: Metric: committed_throughput_utilization (per-contract) - SLO target: >= 95% availability against committed units over 7d
Dashboard: per-region commitment map and shard placement heatmap in Console
testing_plan: Unit tests for allocator math and shard-weight rounding edge cases.
Integration tests with autoscaler and runtime staging cluster to measure cold-start and prewarm behavior.
Chaos test: simulate zone loss and verify staged failback and no residency violations.
Load test: synthetic traffic ramps to validate 90s headroom guarantee for 95% of committed load.
Security test: KMS/HSM integration and audit log tamper checks.
User acceptance: run closed beta with two internal customers (search and summarization teams).
migration_strategy: Backfill: convert existing dedicated reservations to contracts with opt-in negotiation window.
Default headroom: legacy reservations get a conservative headroom profile; customers can opt into tighter guarantees via API.
Safe rollback: contracts can be disabled per-customer to revert to current autoscale behavior; orchestrator supports circuit-breaker in controller.
Data migration: persist contract state in revisioned store with idempotent apply semantics.
decision_notes: We picked a commitment + soft_headroom model (vs hard fixed shard count) to allow better multiplexing and lower cost for bursty tenants.
Prewarm leases implemented at the pod/pool level instead of per-request caching to avoid kernel-level complexity and to reuse existing autoscaling hooks.
Residency enforcement is enforced at admission time with audit logging; explicit cross-region opt-in will require legal review and explicit billing note.

notes_for_support: When a customer reports a residency_violation alert, follow runbook section 'Residency exceptions' to triage: check contract flags, placement decisions, and audit logs.
Beta customers will see a new contract_id field in request logs; support should use this to correlate committed capacity paths.
If scheduled failback occurs, CS should notify customer with event id and timestamp; include link to Console contract timeline.
